ai_assessment.method: Full direct German-to-Vietnamese comparison of all 97 canonical passages and both titles. Separate subagent drafting from the original preceded review. A separate-context assessor (same model family, not shown the drafter’s notes or scores) read every pair first and reported 1 major and 14 minor findings with a pre-revision weighted score of 8.85; the drafter revised the text, re-read the changed passages and the whole target for naturalness, then assigned these final scores bound to the final byte hashes.
ai_assessment.limitations: The same AI system drafted, revised and assessed the work; the separate-context pass is correlated same-model feedback, not independent review or model diversity. No human literary reviewer, native-reader trial or measured reader demand is claimed. Existing Vietnamese translations were not consulted or collated. Scores are subjective and uncalibrated; missed errors may remain. Source clearance is separately recorded and is not granted by this review.

findings.explanation: Grete’s pronoun shift for Gregor (es → er in ‘er fängt schon wieder an’ and over the corpse in 3.31) had been flattened to nó; now anh ấy where she says er, nó where she says es.
Cross-part consistency: tàu điện (2.2/3.38); the father’s self-reference bố (2.29); Kommis as nhân viên bán hàng (3.7).
Grete’s ‘Du, Gregor!’ restored as a threat (Anh… Gregor!); the mother’s ‘Mọi người’ (2.19); Endlich as Thế là xong! (3.28).
Calques fixed: der große Schnitt (1.5), verfolgen (1.18), sich aussöhnen (3.9), Doppelkinn (2.29), Dienermütze (3.19); the lieutenant’s quân phục (1.26); German-style ‘–,’ punctuation removed.
Endlich! as Thế là xong! keeps the release but loses some of the sense of ‘at last’.

summary: Full assessment of all 97 German/Vietnamese passages and both titles. Gregor’s waking as vermin, the chief clerk’s visit, the family’s first horror, Grete’s feeding, the removal of the furniture, the apple, the lodgers, the violin, Grete’s verdict, Gregor’s death and the family’s tram ride into the countryside are complete in every clause of Kafka’s long sentences. Three parts drafted separately were harmonised; the separate-context pass found one major issue (Grete’s es/er shift flattened) and fourteen minor ones, all revised. Fidelity, voice, imagery and mechanics are 9.0, naturalness 8.5. Unrounded weighted score 8.925 meets the unchanged 8.6 threshold. No unresolved major or critical issue remains.

title_review.rationale: Hóa thân is the established, sober Vietnamese title and matches cuộc hóa thân in the text; it avoids the more sensational Biến dạng.
